references: Diderot & d'Alembert, Encyclopédie — plates of the mechanical arts (craft engravings; plate-caption grammar) → `plate` treatment + in-SVG Latin inscriptions + figcaptions.
Descartes, La Géométrie (1637) — ruled geometric diagrams, letter-labeled figures, recast shapes → the grid's own visual language for p2c11–p2c13 (quoted, then cracked).

Neurath/Arntz Isotype (Vienna Method, 1925–34) — flat pictograms, no perspective, repetition not enlargement → tool-shadow grammar for p2c7–p2c10 + p2c14–p2c16; keeps workshop scenes out of stock-illustration rendering.
Hereford Mappa Mundi (c. 1300) — lived cartography, oriented use-labeled space, center-by-meaning → p2c14–p2c16 region art (places by use, region glowing when something is missing).
